claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to sustain a protective oxide above 900 °C is governed by oxidation synergy between Cr and X.
Al oxidation produces a slow-growing Al2O3 layer.
The Al2O3 layer has low growth strain.
Al2O3 couples with a Cr-rich oxide to form a duplex scale.
The proposed duplex scale minimizes oxide-growth stresses.
The proposed duplex scale minimizes thermal-expansion mismatch.
Oxides formed in the Si- or Mn-containing alloys grow more rapidly or generate greater mismatch strain than the proposed Al-containing duplex scale.
Rapid oxide growth or high mismatch strain initiates cracking and spallation.
The protective scale is primarily Cr-rich, for example Cr2O3, with a secondary oxide layer such as Al2O3 in the Al-containing alloy.
The proposed composite scale has reduced oxygen diffusivity.
The proposed composite scale has a coefficient of thermal expansion better matched to the substrate.
Reduced oxygen diffusivity and improved thermal-expansion matching maintain interfacial coherence.
In CrFeCoNiAl, tandem Al2O3 and Cr2O3 formation alleviates tensile-stress accumulation that would otherwise cause cracking.
Under identical high-temperature exposure, CrFeCoNiAl will have fewer oxide microcracks than CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn.
Under identical high-temperature exposure, CrFeCoNiAl will exhibit less oxide spallation than CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn.
CrFeCoNiAl will form a slower-growing oxide scale than CrFeCoNiSi or CrFeCoNiMn.
Si- and Mn-containing alloys will form less adherent oxide scales than the Al-containing alloy.
Previous reports found unstable, cracking oxides in some CrFeCoNiX compositions.
Changes in processing, composition, or thermal history can affect oxide-growth kinetics and stress development.
